title: Game Map Viewer — game.json
description: Contract for a single game's map configuration, produced by nes_decoder and consumed by the map_viewer web app. See CONTRACT.md.

id.description: Stable game identifier. Must match the registry entry and the res/{id}/ folder name.

version.description: Optional contract version this file was produced against (currently 1). Lets a future breaking change be detected instead of silently misread.

defaultMap.description: Key in `maps` shown first and treated as the navigation root (usually "world_map").

data.description: Optional external catalogs relative to this game.json folder.

items.description: Item catalog JSON path, e.g. data/items.json.

services.description: Shop/service catalog JSON path, e.g. data/services.json.

species.description: Species catalog JSON path, e.g. data/species.json.

parties.description: Battle party catalog JSON path, e.g. data/parties.json.

trainers.description: Trainer catalog JSON path, e.g. data/trainers.json.

currencies.description: Currency catalog JSON path, e.g. data/currencies.json.

export.description: Provenance stamp written automatically at export time — identifies which export (and which decoder iteration) produced this data. Shown in the viewer's build-identifier chip.

producer.description: Producing tool + its git sha, e.g. "nes_decoder@4b3941b".

rom.description: Short hash of the source ROM, e.g. "sha1:9f2a01c4".

poiKinds.description: Optional display metadata for this game's POI kinds — legend name + glyph ship with the data, so new kinds need no viewer update. Kinds absent here fall back to the viewer's built-ins.

localizedString.description: Display text keyed by language code. At least one entry required; `en` is the fallback.

type.description: Render mode: a single image, or a pre-rendered tile pyramid (tilesPath).

image.description: Path to the map image, relative to this game.json's folder (res/{id}/).

thumbnail.description: Optional low-res placeholder for progressive loading. Only used when `width` and `height` are also present.

width.description: Optional intrinsic pixel width of `image`. Lets the viewer skip probing the full image.

tileSize.description: Tile size in pixels; drives the grid overlay and the editor's snap-to-grid. Typically 16.

floorGroup.description: Optional building/dungeon key: maps sharing it are floors of one place and get an in-map floor switcher. Must be STABLE across re-exports (derive from map table facts, not enumeration order).

floor.description: Floor number within `floorGroup` (1 = ground, negative = basement: -1 renders B1F). Drives switcher order and labels.

tilesPath.description: Tile URL template for type=tiles, relative to the game res dir (e.g. world_tiles/{z}/{x}_{y}.png); latlng space stays full-res pixels.

minNativeZoom.description: Lowest pre-rendered pyramid level for type=tiles (default -5).

jumps.description: Non-spatial map jumps shown in the sidebar when exact trigger coordinates are unknown.

pois.description: Points of interest (treasure chests, etc.) shown as icons.

events.description: Event-driven tile changes (e.g. a wall opening); each is a toggleable overlay.

jump.description: A map-to-map navigation item without a clickable spatial bounds rectangle.

target.description: Key of the destination map within this same game's `maps`.

kind.description: Optional jump semantics, e.g. warp, door, shortcut.

focus.description: Optional target pixel focus [x, y], full-resolution image space.

event.description: A terrain change a map applies when a story event fires; toggled by a checkbox in the viewer.

overlay.description: Path to the changed-tiles overlay image, relative to this game.json's folder.

tiles.description: Number of tiles this event changes.

trigger.description: A clickable zone that navigates to another map (a door / exit / warp).

target.description: Key of the destination map within this same game's `maps`, or __return__ for a return-stack exit.

kind.description: Optional trigger semantics, e.g. door, exit, or return.

returnTargets.description: Candidate source maps for a return-stack exit when no navigation context exists.

focus.description: Optional target pixel focus [x, y], full-resolution image space.

poi.description: A point of interest on a map (e.g. a treasure chest).

pos.description: Pixel position [x, y] (top-left of the tile), full-resolution image space.

item.description: Optional item id/hex for treasure POIs.

icon.description: Optional sprite image path (relative to the game's res dir); rendered as the marker instead of a glyph, on every map.

iconSize.description: Native pixel size [w, h] of `icon` (defaults to [16, 32]).

itemIcon.description: Optional item mini-icon: relative image path for ROM bag icons, or emoji:<glyph> when no item icon graphics exist. Shown in the tooltip, treasure panel and checklist — not as a map marker.

items.description: Explicit contents for a POI that yields multiple items. Each item can carry its own name, raw id, and mini-icon.

itemRefs.description: Canonical item references for this POI. The viewer resolves names/prices/icons from data/items.json.

currencyRefs.description: Canonical currency/money references for this POI. The viewer resolves names/icons/formatting from data/currencies.json.

speciesId.description: Stable species/entity id in data/species.json for standalone encounters.

hidden.description: True when the collectible has NO visible sprite in the rendered map image (buried / Itemfinder-style items). Only these get an attention glyph in the viewer; visible chests rely on their baked-in sprite + a hover zone.

party.description: Optional structured battle party (a trainer's Pokémon, an enemy general's army…); the viewer renders it as an icon/name/badge card in the tooltip and makes the POI markable. Full roster, in battle order — do not truncate.

reward.description: Optional defeat reward (prize money, spoils…), pre-formatted (e.g. "¥624"). Shown dimmed in the party-card header.

partyId.description: Stable battle party id in data/parties.json.

serviceIds.description: Optional references to game-wide services/shops attached to this map POI.

item.description: Optional item id/hex for this contained item.

itemIcon.description: Optional item mini-icon for this contained item: image path or emoji:<glyph>.

amountRange.description: Inclusive min/max range, when the game rolls a random amount.

partyMember.description: One member of a POI's battle party, rendered as an icon · name · badge row.

value.description: Numeric badge, right-aligned (a level, a troop count…). Omit for a name-only row.

unit.description: Localized badge prefix shown dimmed before `value`. Default "Lv" — e.g. {"zh": "兵"} renders 兵12000.

id.description: Optional game-internal id of this member (species / general id), for debugging/stability.

icon.description: Optional mini-icon path (relative to the game's res dir). Missing icon → the viewer shows a placeholder; the row layout is unaffected.

bounds.description: Axis-aligned rectangle in FULL-RESOLUTION image pixels: [[x1, y1], [x2, y2]], top-left origin.

saveFormat.description: Optional save-file layout enabling battery-save import. Interpreted by the viewer together with each POI's `saveRef`. See CONTRACT.md §Save import.

family.description: Save-format family the viewer's parser dispatches on, e.g. "nes-sram".

size.description: Accepted raw file size(s) in bytes; import rejects any other size.

regions.description: Named bitfield regions; a POI's `saveRef.region` selects one (default "treasure").

bitOrder.description: Bit order within each byte: "lsb" (bit 0 = 0x01) or "msb". Default "lsb".

signature.description: Optional signature byte checks confirming the save belongs to this game.

saveFlagRegion.description: A contiguous bitfield inside the save file (e.g. the opened-chest bits).

offset.description: Byte offset of the bitfield within the raw save file.

length.description: Length of the bitfield in bytes.

saveSignature.description: A byte-signature check confirming a save belongs to this game.

offset.description: Byte offset of the signature within the save file.

hex.description: Expected bytes as a lowercase hex string, e.g. "4d4554".

saveRef.description: Which save-file flag proves this POI is done (chest opened, boss beaten…).

flag.description: Bit index within the region: byte = flag >> 3, bit = flag & 7.
